body: Valley Post is a four-building dining development off Dunnavant Valley Road in Chelsea, Alabama, in Shelby County south of Birmingham. A Birmingham developer built it, and its only operator was a Pihakis Restaurant Group affiliate. It housed four concepts: Hero Diner, Luca & Lucy, Little Donkey and Rodney Scott BBQ. According to court documents described by AL.com, the development opened in December 2025, and no rent was paid from that month on.

In April 2026 the Pihakis Restaurant Group began closing restaurants, and all four Valley Post restaurants shut. That month the landlord side filed liens on several properties leased to the group and its affiliates. WBRC reported that the amended Valley Post lien, filed April 27, claimed $7,166,296.20 plus attorney fees and other expenses for rent due under the leases. In June, the landlord entity, Dunnavant Valley Dining LLC, sued in Shelby County Circuit Court. It alleged that PRG Valley Post had defaulted on a long-term lease of the four buildings, with charges totaling about $7.35 million.

The tenant never answered, and the court entered a default judgment for $7.19 million in unpaid rent, attorney fees and court costs, as AL.com reported on October 7, 2026. According to that report, the court certified the judgment as final, which makes it immediately enforceable, and post-judgment interest accrues until it is paid.

Published reporting does not say how the judgment will be collected, whether the leases carried guaranties, or how the award was calculated against the roughly $7.35 million originally claimed. Waldo's Chicken and Beer opened a Valley Post location on September 29, and Saw's BBQ is expected to open there later this fall.
